He had joined the army in 1920 fresh from Raider's Wood 34th out of his class of 201, down from 225 because of that damned scandal the year before. Some good cadets had checked out and threatened to tear up their papers in protest, some daft bastards actually did it, but when General Ekwall was raked over the goals by the media it was done. Deke Sawyer, sorry, Captain Deke Sawyer, didn't even care about half the stuff people were all up in arms about; it was just the damned principle of the matter that rubbed him wrong. Ekwall had earned his chops during the Red Summer of 1904, he showed those commies and sociarists what for, and then he showed what he could do in 1912 when the Islands War broke out. That just made it sweeter when the journalists sunk their teeth in, they loved the taste of hero.

Thinking of Ekwall made him wonder about his own career, he had just earned his shiny new rank and there was talk about cutting half the army back! Hell, half the whole damned military! Those morons up in Harrisburg were making all the wrong decisions, 1921 was just the start and it didn't stop. Those damned reds! Eight damned years of service and now they were drumming him out, he was sure of it, and with the new war across the Hibernic it couldn't have come at a worse time! Oh if his father was still alive he'd be absolutely livid, the old man was probably rolling in his grave.

A loud pop made Deke jump in place, his head snapped around as the source of the noise roared overhead trailing thick smoke from two of it's engines. Another bomber from... Lendia by the look of it, the red and white eagle crest it wore on the fuselage was missing it's head; a cannon round had taken care of that. Apparently the bomber's comrades were taken care of too, aside from lingering smoke the sky was empty. Somewhere to the south he imagined some hotshot pilot was laughing it in Espanian with his buddies, or maybe it was a gun crew having a drink of tequila or rum.

He envied them, even if they were on the wrong side.

More planes roared above, he recognized their make as B-11 Sultans that were probably in Aerigan inventory at one time, but those fools in the Capitol Building sold off the entire damned Air Corps! At least they were more friends, for some damned reason it wasn't okay to shoot the Reds down when they flew in. Apparently everyone had forgotten what the Reds did when they took over Sarova and Vicoppar, what they tried to do wherever they went, but the Sawyers hadn't; oh no, his granddad made damned sure Deke grew up knowing the score.

"Captain!"

Deke stopped and turned around, returning the salute. "Yes, corporal?"

Holding out the official-looking letter, the corporal inhaled deeply and said, "sir, I was told to get this to you right away."

"Catch your breath, let's see what's in here..."

He read the first few lines quickly, the words "regret" and "promotion" popped out, followed by "not at this time." Damn them! Now it was the damned pencil pushers in the Defense Department screwing him over, he wasn't being drummed out he was losing his command one papercut at a time. None of his recommendations were approved, when he read the rest it made him damned sick! Down to a hundred men in his company, "budget constraints" of course!

"You're dismissed, corporal. Thank you," he muttered, returning the enlisted man's salute. So they were having corporals run errands now, what a damned joke!

Pencil pushers and politicians, they would be the death of the federation for sure. They weren't even hiding their agenda anymore, and what's worse is the people loved them for it! No matter how hard he tried he couldn't get through to anyone, everyone was so damned happy about all the money flowing in. Most of the military had kept their old ways, they knew this "era of peace" was a farce, a rotten charade, cooked up by those greedy fools running the nation. A people couldn't get by with selling all their guns, planes, and bombs to the rest of the world and then expect the victors to keep from turning on them.

When he got inside the office it was abuzz with activity, unusual for the time of day. All those secretaries who usually scattered the moment the day's work was done had been pressed into service typing up a whole lot of something, he had never heard so many typewriters running at once. Across the hall he saw the telegraph tickers spitting out ribbons of paper, the operators writing furiously to keep up. Boy he did not envy those guys!

"Sawyer! Get in here!"

Doing as he was told, he stepped inside the office and closed the door to dim the noise. There wasn't a need to salute, he just answered, "yes, sir?"

"I take it you heard the news?" Colonel Pierce grunted, Deke noticed a letter similar to his own in the trash. "I'll tell you what it is, it's a goddamn tragedy."

"Yes, sir. I was hoping they would see the wisdom in-"

"Ha! Good luck, we're short on that these days," he muttered, holding out a new piece of paper. "Sit down before you read that, latest news."

With a warning like that who could argue? He couldn't help himself, his eyes gobbled up the juicy details as he slid into the seat. Fifteen dead, thirty four wounded from an "incident" at sea! No details on the ship itself, but she caught a torpedo just outside Aerigan waters amidship. Another report had a pair of Talentican fighters chasing a bomber into their airspace, some P-29s of the East Berylina State Guard sent them packing but the damage was done. Six civilians just so happened to be in the way when that bomber came down!

Hiding his smile he passed the paper back. "So does this mean we're...?"

"No. Damn it, no, I just got off the phone with General Thompson and apparently it's 'a diplomatic issue.'"

Hearing that made his heart sink, for a brief moment he tasted that hope and it was snatched from him in an instant. When the morning paper would hit the streets they would have egg on their face again and nobody would bother, a few people might get angry but damn it nothing would happen!

"If that won't do it then what will? What the hell will it take, sir?"

Colonel Pierce shook his head and scowled, chewing on his cigar. "Hell if I know, Sawyer. Get out of here, go tell your men the bad news."
